summary: Practise satellite scene screening, environmental indicator mapping, and field-verification planning. Explore this five-day course outline.
lede: Remote sensing for environmental monitoring uses satellite observations to track environmental conditions and guide monitoring decisions. For environmental officers, GIS analysts, and monitoring coordinators, the course develops repeatable workflows that connect monitoring questions to evidence and field checks. Practise selecting and screening Sentinel-2 or Landsat scenes in SNAP, calculating and interpreting environmental indicators, comparing season-matched observations, and documenting uncertainty in QGIS maps and evidence briefs.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who use environmental observations, satellite imagery, or field surveys to plan monitoring and communicate evidence. It suits foundation-level learners who want to add repeatable satellite workflows to their current responsibilities.
audience: Natural Resource Planning Officers using satellite trends
prerequisites: Basic computer use and familiarity with environmental monitoring terms are useful. No remote-sensing experience or coding is required. Bring a laptop with QGIS and SNAP installed; the exercises use sample satellite imagery and do not require a software account.
